notes: [2026-09-07T08:03:38+00:00] Perf beacon run 2 analysed. The regression between run 1 and run 2 is NOT in repo code: untouched CPU probes got slower per unit of work (occluder cull 1.59x, depth sort 1.33x), run1w5 and run2w5 have identical CPU busy (29.26 vs 29.21 ms/frame) but run 2 has a fifth the occluders and +20 ms/frame idle. That is the phone thermally throttling, not the game. The four lighting commits cut the lighting block 293.1 -> 181.4 ms per second of wall (-38%). New this run: the mist and depth-fog passes were running every frame while OFF (Phaser's Shader.willRender returns true unconditionally for render-to-texture shaders, so setVisible(false) does nothing) - mist dispatched a full-canvas program 9,534 times across both runs to write vec4(0). Fixed by taking passes off the display list. Any domain that ever adds a full-screen Phaser shader pass: setVisible is not an off switch.

[2026-09-08T23:19:25+00:00] Running-into-a-new-area lag FOUND and FIXED (games2 c402d81ebd, confirmed by the maintainer on his phone: '0 lag'). Cause: Phaser 3.90's single autoResize capture RenderTarget is deleted and re-created on every DynamicTexture bracket whose size differs from the previous one; ground RT 1510x1656 vs cover atlases 1024x512 vs light fields 544x708 meant ~12 MB of VRAM freed and re-allocated twice per slice frame once scenery was on. client/src/capturepool.ts keeps one non-resizing target per size. Lesson for every domain that draws into a DynamicTexture/RenderTexture: a new SIZE is a per-frame re-allocation on stock Phaser; the pool makes it a one-time cost. createTextureFromSource(null,w,h) returns in 0.1 ms because the driver only queues the allocation - the cost lands in the GPU process later, in nobody's timer.
